headline: Dance Team Foundation
threshold: Use Spanish to complete the Dance Team situations, ask for clarification, and confirm a shared plan.

lessons.title: Meet your dance team
lessons.objective: Introduce yourself to a new teammate, ask their name, and explain that you are new.
lessons.focus: Use ser for identity and descriptions; estar for location or current state. Spanish subject pronouns are often optional.

words.en: I am new to the team.
Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Introduce yourself to a new teammate, ask their name, and explain that you are new. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: ¡Hola! Soy tu compañera, Ana. ¿Cómo te llamas?

lessons.title: Find your place in the studio
lessons.objective: Ask where to leave your belongings and describe a clear space to rehearse.
lessons.focus: Hay means there is or there are. Use está/están to locate a specific person or item.

words.en: Where do I leave my backpack?
Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Ask where to leave your belongings and describe a clear space to rehearse. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: Hay espacio junto a la pared. ¿Dónde quieres dejar tu mochila?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: Count an eight-count
lessons.objective: Count a phrase, identify the pause, and ask to start again.
lessons.focus: Use cuánto for how much, cuántos for how many masculine items, and a qué hora for at what time.

words.en: Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Count a phrase, identify the pause, and ask to start again. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: Vamos a contar ocho tiempos. ¿Puedes contar conmigo?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: Right, left, front and back
lessons.objective: Confirm whose right or left is meant before changing your position.
lessons.focus: State whose perspective is used. A la derecha de locates something to the right of a reference; hacia indicates direction.

words.en: Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Confirm whose right or left is meant before changing your position. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: Mira hacia el espejo. ¿Cuál es tu derecha ahora?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: Talk about movement
lessons.objective: Identify body-part vocabulary and check that you understood a movement cue.
lessons.focus: Tener expresses possession. Tener + noun is also used in expressions such as tener una duda.

words.en: Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Identify body-part vocabulary and check that you understood a movement cue. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: Señala tu hombro y tu rodilla. ¿Qué palabras quieres practicar?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: Ask the coach to repeat
lessons.objective: Ask a specific clarification question and request slower speech without leaving Spanish.
lessons.focus: Use question words with their written accents: qué, cómo, cuál, dónde and cuándo. Include both Spanish question marks.

words.en: Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Ask a specific clarification question and request slower speech without leaving Spanish. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: Te explico el paso en español. ¿Qué parte quieres que repita?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: What to bring to rehearsal
lessons.objective: Ask what to bring and tell a teammate what you still need.
lessons.focus: Necesitar can be followed by a noun or an infinitive. The second verb stays in its dictionary form.

words.note: Common in Mexico and parts of Latin America; also zapatos deportivos or zapatillas.
In this hair context, a hair tie; also goma or gomita in other regions.

words.en: What do I have to bring?
Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Ask what to bring and tell a teammate what you still need. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: Mañana tenemos ensayo. ¿Ya tienes todo en tu bolsa?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: Rehearsal days and times
lessons.objective: Confirm the rehearsal day, arrival time, and departure time.
lessons.focus: Use a las with most clock times; a la una is singular. Days follow el for one specified day and los for a repeated schedule.

words.en: Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Confirm the rehearsal day, arrival time, and departure time. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: El viernes cambiamos de horario. ¿A qué hora puedes llegar?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: Describe the music you like
lessons.objective: Give a musical preference and explain it politely.
lessons.focus: Me gusta is used with one thing or an activity; me gustan with plural things. The thing liked determines the verb.

words.en: Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Give a musical preference and explain it politely. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: ¿Te gusta más el jazz o el hiphop? ¿Por qué?
lessons.partnerRole: a supportive dance coach or teammate

lessons.title: Your first complete rehearsal
lessons.objective: Walk a new teammate through a rehearsal and ask for one useful review.
lessons.focus: Primero, después and al final organize actions. Antes de and después de are followed by a noun or an infinitive.

words.en: Can you repeat it more slowly?
I want to confirm that I understood.

lessons.speaking: Walk a new teammate through a rehearsal and ask for one useful review. Speak in Spanish; ask for help or slower speech when needed. End by confirming the agreed next step.
lessons.openingLine: Hoy voy a ser tu nueva compañera. ¿Qué hacemos primero?
